examples.purpose: A portfolio allocation, the guide's In context: a Card gives the portfolio label and its explanation, and the chart owns the category comparison. The values are percentages of the portfolio on a shared 0–100 scale (max 100): Small & Mid is 65% now against a recommended 35%, and Large (25%) and Others (10%) have no recommendation. The bar area is 138 px.
examples.jsx:
<Card>
  <Card.Title>Portfolio allocation</Card.Title>
  <Card.SupportText>Current mix compared with the recommended reference</Card.SupportText>
  <AllocationComparisonChart
    data={[
      { label: 'Small & Mid', value: 65, baseline: 35 },
      { label: 'Large', value: 25 },
      { label: 'Others', value: 10 },
    ]}
    max={100}
    height={138}
  />
</Card>

from.quote: A Card can provide the portfolio label and explanation while the chart owns the category comparison.

notes: Extracted 31 October 2026 from the guide (src/guides/allocationcomparisonchart.guide.tsx, which only registers src/AllocationComparisonChartGuide.tsx, where the content is) and docs/evidence/allocationcomparisonchart.md at 31f1c5e (“docs: add onboarding home page, component search, and favicon”, 29 September), an ancestor of origin/main; the three files are the same on origin/main and origin/docs-next. The guide's Sources note (“Checked 22 September 2026”, “exports from jfs-components 0.1.60”) and the evidence's Batch check (22 September, declared and resolved 0.1.60) were checked on 0.1.60, and the guide has had no 0.1.78 check. So only the guide body (summary, core principle, Anatomy, Configuration, States, Sizing, Content, In context, Do & Don'ts) is quoted for guidance, and the one item resting on the Sources note, /facts/gaps/0 (the clipped baseline), carries 2026-09-22 and 0.1.60 and stays flagged by the trace check: no guide-body sentence or later check carries it. Installed build: jfs-components 0.1.78, mirror v0.1.78-dbe0e02 (Biscuit's main at dbe0e02, 27 October). The mirror's history starts at 0.1.77 (1f05631, 28 September), so 0.1.60 was read upstream (MrBiscuit/react-native-storybook-boilerplate-master, “Release v0.1.60”, e02346e, 30 July) through gh api. Builds compared (blob SHAs): AllocationComparisonChart.tsx is 7b9c364 at upstream 0.1.60, unchanged upstream since 7833d2e (v0.1.12, June), at v0.1.77, v0.1.78, -636f3f5, -c7d3348 and -dbe0e02, and in node_modules. MetricLegendItem.tsx (the legend items) is 5a46fd2 at 0.1.60 and eb7c1e2 from upstream 0.1.65 (0af3eb7) to dbe0e02; the only change wraps the label and value line heights in safeTextLineHeight (12 px text on a 16 px line stays 16). react-utils.ts (bd10632), figma-variables-resolver.ts (d03e77c) and JFSThemeProvider.tsx (fa8a86a) are the same blobs at 0.1.60 and dbe0e02; figma-modes.generated.ts changed, but its AllocationComparisonChart and MetricLegendItem lines (Appearance / DataViz, Color Mode, Emphasis / DataViz) read the same. The Coin Variables file is 71587b0 at 0.1.60 and 4545aec on dbe0e02; all 33 segmentIndicator/*, allocationComparisonChart/* and metricLegendItem/* variables have the same values in both. So nothing the 22 September check read has changed, and every guide sentence quoted here was read against the installed source (read, not rendered; token values through the package's own getVariableByName in lib/commonjs): the container is 100% wide (AllocationComparisonChart.tsx line 388); the legend row shows Current, and Recommended only when some segment has a baseline (389–411); bars sit in a row with role image, 8 px apart (413–419); each bar's height is height × value / max, held between 0 and the full bar area, with max defaulting to the largest value or baseline (349–355, 420–422); height defaults to 154 and excludes the value and caption rows (295; the height fact); the bar width is segmentIndicator/track/width, 28, unless barWidth is set, with fully rounded ends (radius 99999, capped at half the width) (314–317); the baseline overlay is drawn from the bottom of the bar at min(baseline height, bar height) (196–198, 222–233), and its dashed 1 px white marker and label sit at the top of the overlay, on the first segment with a baseline unless a segment sets its own marker (234–262, 440–441); the value above each bar and the caption below are one line each (205–209, 268–270), 12 px on a 12 px line, weight 400, rgb(12, 13, 16); bar fill rgb(93, 0, 181), overlay rgb(184, 79, 189); formatValue defaults to `${v}%` (300); the chart has no press handler or state anywhere. No guide sentence quoted here is contradicted. Not current and not quoted: the Sources “Examples use public AllocationComparisonChart and AllocationSegment exports from jfs-components 0.1.60” and the evidence's batch line (the version is stale; every prop the guide's examples pass, data, max, height, showLegend, modes, accessibilityLabel and style, and every segment field they use, label, value, baseline and showMarker, still exists on dbe0e02), reported to the coordinator as a candidate guide fix (re-check on 0.1.78 and update the Sources note). The clipped baseline still holds on dbe0e02 and also shows in Storybook's BaselineEverywhere story (upstream stories at dbe0e02: Large 25 against 40, Others 10 against 25): the overlay, and with a marker the dashed line and its label (“40%”), stop at the top of the shorter bar. It is recorded as /facts/gaps/0 and reported to the coordinator as a Component Bug candidate; no ticket on the board reports it (all 543 tickets searched, read only; Codex's 22 September comment on Documentation #146 calls it a documented package limitation). Facts: the facts generator lists the fields of row types whose name ends in Item, so AllocationSegment's fields (key, label, value, baseline, showMarker, valueLabel, baselineLabel, color, baselineColor, accessibilityLabel) are not facts; the entry names a segment's value, baseline and label in plain words, as the data fact does, and the examples use only those three (reported to the coordinator). The component's JSDoc (the facts' doc) and the barWidth fact describe the bars with a shape word Coin doesn't use (AllocationComparisonChart.tsx 17, 85, 175, 276 and 286, listed in #544, Component Fix, To do, Biscuit); nothing hand-written here repeats it, and the guide's own word for a bar, pillar, stays in the anatomy part name Current pillar and in the quoted Sources sentence. Storybook's MDX and stories (upstream at dbe0e02) use the same word (not in #544's list; reported). Modes: the facts list Appearance / DataViz (default Primary), Emphasis / DataViz (default High) and Color Mode. On dbe0e02 none of them changes anything the chart draws: the segmentIndicator/* and allocationComparisonChart/* variables are single-mode (“Segment Indicator / Output”) and the legend's label tokens resolve the same in every mode (checked for every Appearance / DataViz and Emphasis / DataViz value and Color Mode Dark), although the Storybook MDX says Appearance and Emphasis retint the fills (reported; Dark mode is not recorded here). Strength: two quotes hold “only”: /configuration/1 “A recommended value appears only when the data includes a baseline.” (everywhere: behaviour, so recommended) and /configuration/3 “Omit the reference when the page only needs current category amounts.” (contextual: the word sets the page's condition). Nothing is required: the guide has no everywhere-scoped instruction, and the package requires no prop (data falls back to a built-in Small & Mid, Large, Others sample when left out, lines 120–124 and 293; not recorded). avoidWhen rests on the States description (no selected or pressed state); the guide names no other component to use instead, so no rule carries useInstead. Anatomy required: the Current pillar and the Category label are drawn for every segment; the Legend can be hidden (showLegend), and the Baseline overlay and the Marker need a baseline. Examples follow the building rules: no Color Mode, and no Appearance / DataViz or Emphasis / DataViz (the guide sets Light, Primary and High on every chart; Primary and High are the defaults and, on dbe0e02, change nothing); no style (the guide's width 100% is the container's default) and no accessibilityLabel (the guide's are built from its playground preset, such as “allocation allocation comparison chart”; left out, the package names the chart from the data, 373–385); the guide's AllocationExample helper is written out with its data (65, 25 and 10, a 35 baseline on Small & Mid) and max 100 (its fixed scale), and showMarker is left out (the first baseline gets the marker by default). The In context Card drops the guide's Color Mode Light, AppearanceBrand Neutral and width style, which the guide doesn't explain; Card has an entry and is used with Card.Title and Card.SupportText as the guide does. The guide's “Shared 0–100 scale” and “Automatic scale from supplied values” captions are page text under each chart, not Coin, and are left out. Left out of examples (three at most): the anatomy specimen, the States cards, the Sizing wide and narrow hosts, the Content example, the Do & Don't previews and the playground. Not recorded: barWidth, valueLegendLabel, disableTruncation, style, chartStyle and legendStyle (no guide sentence; the building rules forbid style overrides of colour, border, radius and font); a segment's per-bar colours (the Sources note: no custom segment colors), value and baseline label overrides and accessibility label; the evidence's Figma node, review image and anatomy-measurement notes; the Storybook story ids the Sources note lists (not re-checked); the one-line truncation of labels and the default accessibility label (source only). Content: good is the guide's short labels; bad is its long Don't labels. Consistency with related entries: ComparisonBar's avoidWhen sends value comparisons to Allocation Comparison Chart and Plan Comparison Card with no useInstead because “neither has an entry”; both now have one (reported to the coordinator; no disagreement in what it says). SegmentedTrack's entry (one whole split into a few parts, a single track) and AreaLineChart's (a continuous trend over time) cover different jobs from this one (category amounts against a reference on one shared scale); none of the three guides names another, and their unit advice agrees (AreaLineChart: the same unit and scale for series people compare; this guide: one unit, one max and one format). No other guidance file names AllocationComparisonChart. Cross-check: round 1 raised no flags. Its notes asked about two items, both resting on facts in this entry: /configuration/10's “showLegend is on by default” is the showLegend fact (default true), and /examples/2's “the height of a bar at the max of 100” is the height fact (“the height of a bar whose value equals max”); the 138 and 220 px heights are the guide's own (In context and Plot height). Left as they are. Sorted by the coordinator: Component Bug #550 (a baseline above its bar is cut off at the bar’s top) and guide fix #553 (re-check on 0.1.78) were filed; /facts/gaps/0 names #550. The cross-check ran again after that (round 2: 1 flag, that the evidence names no bug number), dismissed in reviews/allocationcomparisonchart.json for Astra and Marcin to confirm.
